payload.body_content:
J,

I like the asynchronous model, and I agree there is a useful point
here. Please hold this version, though. I read -00 and the live thread
again. Section 2 explicitly leaves transport and session-establishment
mechanisms out of scope, so saying the draft forces TCP/TLS,
WebSockets, open listeners, or cloud silos would overstate it. Chong
has also already accepted our REQ-3 correction and is replacing
“direct connection” with mechanism-neutral authenticated endpoint
binding.

I think the list contribution should be narrower:

“Chong, one portability clarification for REQ-3: a session association
need not be coextensive with a continuously live transport connection.
Negotiation may be carried synchronously or asynchronously, provided
each message is integrity-protected and bound to both authenticated
endpoint identities, the session, freshness and ordering state, and
the negotiated capability set. Intermediary storage or delivery does
not make the intermediary an authority for either endpoint’s
declarations or selections.”

I would leave DNS-AID and emilia-mailbox out for now. The mailbox repo
is still red at d984101, DNSSEC lookup is not implemented, DNSSEC
authenticates the published record rather than sender authority, and
revocation remains bounded by TTL and cache state.

The asynchronous idea is good. This version will land much better.


Iman
